court: Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm it has Tucker Act jurisdiction over money-mandating military pay and correction claims.

issues.label: Proper defendant
issues.why: The United States must be the correct party for claims seeking money and record correction-related relief.

issues.label: Final agency action
issues.why: The court must determine which Board decision is final and reviewable after remand and de novo review.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply the arbitrary/capricious–contrary to law–substantial evidence standard to the Board record.

issues.label: Scope of record review
issues.why: The court must decide whether review is limited to the administrative record and whether supplementation is permitted.

issues.label: Remand-order compliance
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Board on remand addressed all issues and claims for relief as directed.

issues.label: Issue exhaustion/waiver
issues.why: The court must determine whether any arguments were forfeited by not being raised before the Board.

issues.label: Statute of limitations
issues.why: The court must decide whether each claim is time-barred under the applicable 6-year limitations period.

issues.label: Accrual date: disability retirement
issues.why: The court must determine when a medical retirement/back-pay claim accrued (e.g., separation vs. later Board denial).

issues.label: Accrual date: bonus refund
issues.why: The court must determine when the bonus recoupment claim accrued (recoupment decision/collection vs. discharge).

issues.label: Accrual date: record correction
issues.why: The court must determine when the claim to correct NEC-related entries and narratives accrued (at discharge/NEC action vs. Board denial).

issues.label: Accrual-suspension doctrine
issues.why: The court must decide whether accrual was suspended due to concealment or inability to know essential facts (e.g., narcolepsy not tested).

issues.label: Equitable tolling availability
issues.why: The court must determine whether tolling is legally available and factually justified for any time-barred claims.

issues.label: Continuing-claims doctrine
issues.why: The court must decide whether ongoing retirement pay/back pay creates timely slices even if initial accrual is old.

issues.label: Claim-splitting/res judicata
issues.why: The court must consider whether prior Board decisions, remand proceedings, or earlier court rulings preclude relitigation.

issues.label: Money-mandating entitlement
issues.why: The court must identify the statutes/regulations that mandate pay upon qualifying for disability retirement and apply them.

issues.label: Fitness-for-duty legal test
issues.why: The court must apply the correct legal standard: whether the condition significantly interfered with duties at separation.

issues.label: PEB/MEB referral duty
issues.why: The court must decide whether failure to refer to MEB/PEB violated regulations and whether that legal error was prejudicial.

issues.label: Presumption of fitness
issues.why: The court must consider any presumption that a member separated for reasons other than disability is fit, and whether rebutted.

issues.label: Causation of unfitness
issues.why: The court must decide whether narcolepsy (or other conditions) caused any inability to perform, as opposed to other factors.

issues.label: Evidence at separation
issues.why: The court must decide what contemporaneous evidence shows about functional impact at the time of discharge (evaluations, watchstanding, medical notes).

issues.label: Weight of VA rating
issues.why: The court must decide how much weight to give the VA’s service-connected rating and effective date versus DoD fitness standards.

issues.label: Use of post-service evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether and how post-discharge sleep studies and diagnoses can prove in-service unfitness.

issues.label: Adequacy of Board reasoning
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Board explained its conclusions and connected facts to the fitness determination.

issues.label: Consideration of relevant factors
issues.why: The court must ensure the Board considered all relevant evidence (buddy statements, symptoms, medical opinions, job duties, mishaps).

issues.label: Ignoring contrary evidence
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Board failed to grapple with evidence supporting unfitness or mischaracterized it.

issues.label: Substantial evidence support
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Board’s fit finding is supported by such relevant evidence as a reasonable mind might accept.

issues.label: Reliance on incorrect records
issues.why: The court must assess the impact of the PEB’s initial reliance on another member’s medical records and whether the error tainted the decision.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: Even if procedural or factual error occurred, the court must decide whether it was prejudicial to the outcome.

issues.label: Duty to obtain medical opinion
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board/PEB needed additional medical expertise or testing to decide narcolepsy-related unfitness.

issues.label: Narcolepsy diagnostic standards
issues.why: The court must consider whether lack of in-service MSLT testing undermines the Board’s evaluation of onset and severity.

issues.label: Duty performance vs symptoms
issues.why: The court must determine whether observed sleep episodes equate to duty impairment despite apparently adequate performance evaluations.

issues.label: Safety-sensitive nuclear duties
issues.why: The court must consider the heightened significance of sleep attacks for nuclear watchstanding and whether that affects the fitness analysis.

issues.label: Early separation implications
issues.why: The court must assess whether requesting early separation affects presumptions about fitness or entitlement to disability processing.

issues.label: Separation reason effects
issues.why: The court must consider how an honorable discharge for reduction in force interacts with disability retirement eligibility.

issues.label: Eligibility for PDRL
issues.why: The court must decide whether, if unfit, the condition was permanent/stable enough for PDRL rather than TDRL or separation with severance.

issues.label: Disability rating percentage
issues.why: If unfitness is found, the court must determine the correct disability rating and resulting pay entitlement.

issues.label: Service-connection vs unfitness
issues.why: The court must distinguish VA service-connection from DoD unfitness and apply the correct entitlement framework.

issues.label: Back pay computation
issues.why: The court must determine the proper monetary remedy period, offsets, and calculations if medical retirement is ordered.

issues.label: Offsets and recoupments
issues.why: The court must decide how VA compensation, separation pay, or previously recouped amounts interact with any retirement back pay award.

issues.label: Refund of reenlistment bonus
issues.why: The court must decide whether bonus recoupment was authorized under the reenlistment contract and regulations given the separation circumstances.

issues.label: Bonus recoupment predicate
issues.why: The court must determine whether Mr. Qoye was in fact no longer classified in his rating/NEC or failed to serve the obligated term.

issues.label: Disputed NEC removal fact
issues.why: The court must resolve whether the NEC removal actually occurred and what the official record shows.

issues.label: Basis for NEC removal
issues.why: The court must determine whether NEC removal was properly based on misconduct/unreliability or should be medically based.

issues.label: NJP-to-NEC linkage
issues.why: The court must assess whether the NJP misconduct is an adequate and lawful basis for NEC removal under applicable policies.

issues.label: Misconduct vs medical mitigation
issues.why: The court must decide whether narcolepsy could mitigate the misconduct (false statement/log falsification) for NEC characterization purposes.

issues.label: Record correction authority
issues.why: The court must confirm the Board’s authority and the court’s remedial power to order correction of NEC entries and narratives.

issues.label: Liberal consideration applicability
issues.why: The court must decide whether liberal consideration standards apply to sleep disorder claims and whether honorable discharge affects applicability.

issues.label: Definition of liberal consideration
issues.why: If applicable, the court must decide what evidence must be liberally construed and whether the Board applied the correct approach.

issues.label: Regulatory interpretation
issues.why: The court must interpret governing DoD/SECNAV disability evaluation and NEC classification regulations correctly.

issues.label: Procedural due process
issues.why: The court must consider whether Mr. Qoye received required notice/opportunity regarding NEC removal and disability processing.

issues.label: Arbitrary disparate treatment
issues.why: The court must consider whether similarly situated service members are treated differently in disability/NEC decisions without explanation.

issues.label: Credibility determinations
issues.why: The court must address how the Board evaluated lay statements and whether it provided valid reasons for accepting or rejecting them.

issues.label: Burden of proof standard
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Board used the correct evidentiary burden (e.g., preponderance) and not an impermissibly high standard.

issues.label: Relief specificity
issues.why: The court must decide what precise corrections are required (retirement status, dates, codes, NEC characterization) if relief is warranted.

issues.label: Ancillary equitable relief limits
issues.why: The court must ensure requested relief is within the court’s authority and tied to a money-mandating claim when required.

issues.label: Attorney fees eligibility
issues.why: The court must consider potential entitlement to fees/costs (e.g., EAJA) depending on prevailing party and justification.
